While IFN-γ can recruit neutrophils, Th1 cells are not primarily responsible for this function; instead, they are more directly involved in macrophage activation. Th1 cells do not mediate allergic diseases, which are typically associated with Th2 responses. Therefore, the most accurate statement is that Th1 lymphocytes produce interferon gamma (IFN-γ), which enhances macrophage activation and promotes cell-mediated immunity.
